claims.claim: Quality and good Yamaha keyboard for children
claims.evidence: Subjective quality claim; photos only show casing and wear, not performance.

claims.claim: All keys and buttons working, no dead key, no crackle
claims.evidence: No power-on, audio, or key-press video provided; photos are static and show only dust/wear.
No power adapter visible in any of the three photos; witness explicitly notes its absence.
Provenance claim cannot be confirmed from photos; no import stickers, voltage plate, or UK plug type shown.

risks.risk: Keyboard may not power on or produce sound at all
risks.proof: Video of unit powering on and playing a scale/demo song with audio

risks.risk: Dead, sticky, or unresponsive keys not visible in static photos
risks.proof: Close-up video pressing each key range and showing display response

risks.risk: No power adapter actually present despite seller's claim
risks.proof: Photo of the adapter next to the keyboard with model/voltage label

risks.risk: Hidden damage on back/underside (cracks, battery leakage, broken ports)
risks.proof: Clear photos of rear panel, battery compartment, and all ports
Audio/video clip at moderate volume covering both channels
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified audio quality, risk of crackle

risks.risk: Exact model/age unknown, affecting value and part availability
risks.proof: Clear photo of model/serial sticker, usually on the back
risks.if_unproven: priced at generic low-end PortaSound-era value

proof_requests: Video of keyboard powering on, playing notes across full key range with sound
Photo of the power adapter (with plug type and voltage rating) alongside the unit
Clear photos of the back/underside and battery compartment
Close-up photo of the model/serial number sticker
response.reason: Identity (used Yamaha PortaSound-era keyboard) is settled by the witness, but functionality, adapter presence, and condition claims are unverified or contradicted, so it must be priced at worst case (possible non-functional, no adapter) pending proof.
